title: h3spec HTTP/3 Server Conformance Pipeline Architecture
purpose: Define an advisory h3spec pipeline that tests the local Incursa HTTP/3 server and converts failures into RFC 9114/RFC 9204 triage artifacts.
design_summary: The h3spec pipeline is split into server lifecycle, repo-local tool acquisition, tool invocation, result normalization, and CI dispatch. The server script creates temporary content and TLS materials, starts the local HTTP/3 file server, and writes a server context. The acquisition script downloads the upstream h3spec release under `.artifacts/tools` and emits a Docker wrapper when the host platform cannot run the release binary directly. The runner invokes a configured or acquired h3spec command, captures stdout and stderr, writes metadata, and calls the parser. The parser extracts cases, failures, summary counts, RFC 9114/RFC 9204 section references, and TODO rows. CI runs plan-only by default on pull requests and supports opt-in live execution through workflow dispatch.
edge_cases_and_constraints: The h3spec executable and wrapper arguments must remain configurable because local and hosted environments may install the tool differently.
The repo-local acquisition path must stay under `.artifacts/tools` and must not require global PATH setup.
Parser output must keep raw stdout and stderr as artifacts so parser drift can be diagnosed.
HTTP/3 failures map to RFC 9114 and the `http3-adapter-boundary` gap until narrower protocol-owned requirements exist.
QPACK failures map to RFC 9204 and the `qpack-stream-state-boundary` gap until narrower protocol-owned requirements exist.
Plan-only CI evidence proves the harness shape, not live h3spec conformance.
risks: h3spec output format can drift, so raw logs remain the source of truth.
A passing subset must not be treated as complete RFC 9114 or RFC 9204 support.
Live h3spec installation can be slow or platform-sensitive, so the default pull-request path remains plan-only.
